# Security baseline

<!-- Generated by `cidx security baseline`. Do not edit by hand. -->

What the built-in preset catalogue ships: every container image it runs, pinned
by digest, what those images carry, and every HIGH/CRITICAL finding accepted on
them — with the reason it was accepted and the date that acceptance has to be
argued again.

Carried and accepted are different numbers, and both are stated. A file saying
only what is accepted read "0 accepted findings" on a catalogue carrying 596.
Accepted is a subset of carried: accepting a finding records that it was looked
at, it does not take it out of the image — so the carried count includes what
the audit's ignore file removes from its own scan results (#310).

This file is committed, so its diff is the history of what the catalogue
delivers, and it carries no generation date: the same inputs produce the same
bytes, and a changed line means something actually changed.

Only the built-in catalogue is described here. Presets your own `presets.toml`
declares are yours, and CIDX makes no claim about them (guardrail 1).

An entry past its expiry date waives nothing until it is reviewed; `cidx
security vuln check` is what reports those, and `cidx security vuln prune`
reports the ones no catalogue image carries any more.

**21 images. 241 accepted HIGH/CRITICAL finding(s) across 17 of them.**

## What the images carry

The catalogue carries **1264** HIGH/CRITICAL findings, counted per image — the
same CVE on five images is five repins. They split into four populations:

| Population | Count | What it means |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| Go stdlib in a CLI binary | 131 | Exempt by class: it goes away when the publisher recompiles, and `net/http` is unreachable in a tool that opens no listener. |
| Kernel headers | 256 | Exempt by class: the kernel is the host's, not the container's. The scanner flags the headers package for its version string. |
| Fixed upstream | 647 | A fix exists. This is the images' age, not a decision — an exception must never be written for one. |
| **Needing triage** | **230** | No fix at any version, and not exempt. The only population an exception is the right instrument for. |

None of them is in CISA KEV. The highest EPSS score seen is 0.83. Both are reported
for a human to read; neither gates anything.

These results cannot say what their ignore file took out of them, so the number
above counts only what the scanners still showed: the accepted findings listed
below were removed from their own images' reports by the ignore file the audit
generates from them, and cannot be counted back. Read it as a floor. Trivy keeps
that record under `--show-suppressed` and the audit states how many entries it
wrote alongside its results — generate from its artifacts for the whole number
(#311, #327).

## Images

The **Base** column is the distribution the image is built on, as the scanners
report it. It is here because it decides whether the findings above can ever
go away: once a base stops being supported, its packages receive no further
updates and every finding on that image is permanent, however fresh the tag
is. `none` is an image with no distribution underneath it — a scratch or
static build — which is an answer, not a gap.

The date that support ends is deliberately **not** in this file. It is
relative to the day you read it and it comes from a third party, so it would
change these lines without anything changing about the catalogue — the same
reason there is no generation date. `cidx security baseline` prints it, and
the daily security audit reports it.

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-10536 | CRITICAL | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | CVE-2026-10536 (CRITICAL, curl and libcurl4t64 8.14.1-2+deb13u7, no fix at any version, EPSS 0.00598, not in KEV): a use-after-free when an application sets an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree with CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS or CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E, calls curl_easy_reset, then curl_easy_cleanup. All three are libcurl API calls made by a program embedding the library, in that order, on one handle. The curl command line sets no stream dependency, and cargo-audit's preset runs the tool once for one https download and exits: nothing resets a handle after configuring dependencies. Re-argue if the preset runs anything that embeds libcurl. |

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-107496 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | Unlike the packages in the other decisions, libssl3t64 is used: curl's TLS client opens one https connection to github.com. What each flaw needs is something else. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest: all six are HIGH on openssl, openssl-provider-legacy and libssl3t64 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, not fixed in Debian at any version, none in KEV, EPSS at most 0.006. CVE-2026-107493 needs an application to hand PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex an existing stack and keep using it after a failed read; the PEM it reads here would be the image's own CA bundle, not bytes anyone else chose. CVE-2026-107496 is CMS_encrypt looping on an EC recipient certificate of group order 1; the advisory says TLS and QUIC do not use that path, and nothing here encrypts CMS. CVE-2026-124709 is a QUIC server retaining rejected streams; curl is a client and nothing here listens. CVE-2026-95691 is a use-after-free in the QUIC client on a retransmitted CRYPTO frame, reached only by an HTTP/3 or other QUIC transfer, which needs --http3 and is not requested: the download runs over TCP. CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 are in AES-GCM-SIV, which is not a TLS cipher suite and which no program here calls. Re-argue if the command starts using QUIC, CMS or an OpenSSL application of its own. |

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-107928 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | cargo-audit runs one curl: curl -sSfL -o /tmp/cargo-audit.tgz on a fixed github.com release URL, then checks the archive against a pinned sha256 before tar reads it. The command passes no credentials, proxy, netrc, cookie jar, HSTS file, client certificate, --interface, --proto-default, -J, -w, --aws-sigv4, --crlf, --pinnedpubkey or --parallel, speaks https only, and curl's default redirect protocols are http, https, ftp and ftps; the only server that answers is GitHub's. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest, finding by finding: every one is HIGH, none has a fix at any version, none is in KEV, EPSS at most 0.012. Cookies: CVE-2026-80255 and CVE-2026-82209 (cookie handling) and CVE-2026-92386 (a long cookie record written to a Netscape cookie jar) need the cookie engine, which -b and -c switch on and this command does not. CVE-2026-87862 and CVE-2026-87863 (HSTS import and cache save) need --hsts. Authentication and connection reuse: CVE-2026-8458 (Negotiate connections reused across services), CVE-2026-8932 (client-certificate options left out of the reuse match), CVE-2026-86409 (SigV4 state kept after being unset) and CVE-2026-107929 (CURLOPT_INTERFACE left out of the reuse key) each need an option the command never sets and a handle reused for a second transfer; one handle makes one transfer here. CVE-2026-94266 (credentials in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL) needs credentials in the URL, and the URL carries none. TLS: CVE-2026-80230 (public-key pinning with verification disabled) needs --pinnedpubkey and -k; verification stays on. CVE-2026-9545 (HTTP/3 early data on a cached session) needs --http3 and early data, neither requested. CVE-2026-107928 concerns curl built with GnuTLS sending WebSocket data; the flagged packages are curl and libcurl4t64, Debian's OpenSSL build, and the URL is neither ws:// nor wss://. Other protocols: CVE-2026-13608 (LDAP SASL) and CVE-2026-107161 (Cyrus SASL DIGEST-MD5 client, reached through libcurl's LDAP and mail protocols) need ldap://, imap:// or alike; CVE-2026-87864 (IMAP APPEND with CURLOPT_CRLF), CVE-2026-92387 (control-response timeout of FTP, IMAP, POP3 and SMTP) and CVE-2026-92389 (TFTP state machine) need those servers; CVE-2026-87865 (libssh2 known_hosts), CVE-2026-12064 and CVE-2026-86410 (SSH host verification skipped for a schemeless sftp or scp URL, or after a redirect to one) need an ssh-family transfer: the URL names https, no --proto-default is set, and sftp and scp are outside the default redirect protocols. Tool-only and library-API flaws: CVE-2026-92390 needs --remote-header-name, which the command does not use (it names its output with -o); CVE-2026-9080 (curl_easy_pause inside a CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback), CVE-2026-92391 (a deeply nested MIME tree freed by curl_mime_free) and CVE-2026-80229 (pooled TLS connections outliving their handle) are about an application driving libcurl's API, which the command's single transfer does not. The two CRITICAL curl CVEs this decision used to carry (CVE-2026-18924, CVE-2026-19931) have their own decisions. Re-argue if the command starts using any of these options or protocols. |

Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest: every one is HIGH, none has a fix at any version, none is in KEV, EPSS at most 0.006. libsqlite3-0: CVE-2026-119373 (FTS5 detail=none prefix MATCH over negative rowids), CVE-2026-119374 (FTS5 secure-delete over a corrupted index) and CVE-2026-119379 (sqlite3changeset_apply on crafted changesets) all need a program that opens SQLite databases or applies changesets from outside, and none of the tools here does. gnupg (dirmngr, gpg, gpg-agent, gpgconf, gpgsm, gnupg-l10n): CVE-2026-24882 is a stack overflow in tpm2daemon handling PKDECRYPT for TPM-backed keys; no command runs gpg and a container has no TPM. acl (libacl1): CVE-2026-54369 and CVE-2026-54370 are symlink traversal and a TOCTOU race in the pathname functions, exploitable when a privileged process runs getfacl, setfacl or chacl over a path an attacker controls; nothing here calls them, and tar extracts a sha256-checked archive into /tmp without restoring ACLs. wget: CVE-2026-58469 (Metalink URL underread), CVE-2026-58471 (iconv filename conversion overflow) and CVE-2026-58472 (HTML attribute quoting overflow) need wget to fetch from a hostile server; the preset downloads with curl and never runs wget. ncurses (libncursesw6, libtinfo6, ncurses-base, ncurses-bin): CVE-2025-69720 is a stack overflow in the infocmp tool; nothing runs infocmp. Re-argue if the command starts running any of these. |

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-12064 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | cargo-audit runs one curl: curl -sSfL -o /tmp/cargo-audit.tgz on a fixed github.com release URL, then checks the archive against a pinned sha256 before tar reads it. The command passes no credentials, proxy, netrc, cookie jar, HSTS file, client certificate, --interface, --proto-default, -J, -w, --aws-sigv4, --crlf, --pinnedpubkey or --parallel, speaks https only, and curl's default redirect protocols are http, https, ftp and ftps; the only server that answers is GitHub's. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest, finding by finding: every one is HIGH, none has a fix at any version, none is in KEV, EPSS at most 0.012. Cookies: CVE-2026-80255 and CVE-2026-82209 (cookie handling) and CVE-2026-92386 (a long cookie record written to a Netscape cookie jar) need the cookie engine, which -b and -c switch on and this command does not. CVE-2026-87862 and CVE-2026-87863 (HSTS import and cache save) need --hsts. Authentication and connection reuse: CVE-2026-8458 (Negotiate connections reused across services), CVE-2026-8932 (client-certificate options left out of the reuse match), CVE-2026-86409 (SigV4 state kept after being unset) and CVE-2026-107929 (CURLOPT_INTERFACE left out of the reuse key) each need an option the command never sets and a handle reused for a second transfer; one handle makes one transfer here. CVE-2026-94266 (credentials in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL) needs credentials in the URL, and the URL carries none. TLS: CVE-2026-80230 (public-key pinning with verification disabled) needs --pinnedpubkey and -k; verification stays on. CVE-2026-9545 (HTTP/3 early data on a cached session) needs --http3 and early data, neither requested. CVE-2026-107928 concerns curl built with GnuTLS sending WebSocket data; the flagged packages are curl and libcurl4t64, Debian's OpenSSL build, and the URL is neither ws:// nor wss://. Other protocols: CVE-2026-13608 (LDAP SASL) and CVE-2026-107161 (Cyrus SASL DIGEST-MD5 client, reached through libcurl's LDAP and mail protocols) need ldap://, imap:// or alike; CVE-2026-87864 (IMAP APPEND with CURLOPT_CRLF), CVE-2026-92387 (control-response timeout of FTP, IMAP, POP3 and SMTP) and CVE-2026-92389 (TFTP state machine) need those servers; CVE-2026-87865 (libssh2 known_hosts), CVE-2026-12064 and CVE-2026-86410 (SSH host verification skipped for a schemeless sftp or scp URL, or after a redirect to one) need an ssh-family transfer: the URL names https, no --proto-default is set, and sftp and scp are outside the default redirect protocols. Tool-only and library-API flaws: CVE-2026-92390 needs --remote-header-name, which the command does not use (it names its output with -o); CVE-2026-9080 (curl_easy_pause inside a CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback), CVE-2026-92391 (a deeply nested MIME tree freed by curl_mime_free) and CVE-2026-80229 (pooled TLS connections outliving their handle) are about an application driving libcurl's API, which the command's single transfer does not. The two CRITICAL curl CVEs this decision used to carry (CVE-2026-18924, CVE-2026-19931) have their own decisions. Re-argue if the command starts using any of these options or protocols. |
| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-124709 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | Unlike the packages in the other decisions, libssl3t64 is used: curl's TLS client opens one https connection to github.com. What each flaw needs is something else. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest: all six are HIGH on openssl, openssl-provider-legacy and libssl3t64 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, not fixed in Debian at any version, none in KEV, EPSS at most 0.006. CVE-2026-107493 needs an application to hand PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex an existing stack and keep using it after a failed read; the PEM it reads here would be the image's own CA bundle, not bytes anyone else chose. CVE-2026-107496 is CMS_encrypt looping on an EC recipient certificate of group order 1; the advisory says TLS and QUIC do not use that path, and nothing here encrypts CMS. CVE-2026-124709 is a QUIC server retaining rejected streams; curl is a client and nothing here listens. CVE-2026-95691 is a use-after-free in the QUIC client on a retransmitted CRYPTO frame, reached only by an HTTP/3 or other QUIC transfer, which needs --http3 and is not requested: the download runs over TCP. CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 are in AES-GCM-SIV, which is not a TLS cipher suite and which no program here calls. Re-argue if the command starts using QUIC, CMS or an OpenSSL application of its own. |

A container has no fstab, runs as an unprivileged uid, and no preset here runs mount or nsenter. libsystemd0 (CVE-2026-16742): a systemd-homed local privilege escalation; no systemd runs in a container and nothing here talks to it. perl-base: CVE-2026-82560 is CPU exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document, and nothing here runs pod2text or Pod::Text; CVE-2026-9538 is memory exhaustion in Archive::Tar from an oversized entry size in a tar header, and nothing runs perl: the archive is read by GNU tar, after its sha256 has been checked. glibc: CVE-2026-19499 needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer, and no tool here does; CVE-2026-5435 is the deprecated resolver printing functions ns_printrr, ns_printrrf and fp_nquery writing past a caller-supplied buffer when printing TSIG records, which curl, tar and a Rust binary do not call; CVE-2026-84243 is gettext honouring '/' and '..' in LANGUAGE to load a crafted .mo catalogue, which needs a non-C locale, an attacker-controlled environment and a crafted file on disk: the preset sets no locale variable and nothing here places such a file. libstdc++ (gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6): CVE-2026-102010 (erase_if on libstdc++'s binary-heap priority queue, a GNU pb_ds extension in a header-only template, so the flagged packages hold none of it at run time) and CVE-2026-95619 (an integer overflow in the aligned operator new) both need a C++ program, and none of sh, curl, tar, sha256sum (C) or cargo-audit (Rust) is one. Re-argue if the command starts running an affected tool. |

GSS acceptors and RPC clients: CVE-2026-107778 (a null dereference in gss_accept_sec_context when it receives mismatched KRB-CRED arrays: curl only initiates), CVE-2026-112314 (a leak in clnttcp_call, used by GSS-RPC client programs such as kadmin, which are not here), CVE-2026-118380 (an active attacker altering arguments to RPC services protected by RPCSEC_GSS: no such service or client runs here). Re-argue if the command starts authenticating with Kerberos or running a krb5 program. |

A container has no fstab, runs as an unprivileged uid, and no preset here runs mount or nsenter. libsystemd0 (CVE-2026-16742): a systemd-homed local privilege escalation; no systemd runs in a container and nothing here talks to it. perl-base: CVE-2026-82560 is CPU exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document, and nothing here runs pod2text or Pod::Text; CVE-2026-9538 is memory exhaustion in Archive::Tar from an oversized entry size in a tar header, and nothing runs perl: the archive is read by GNU tar, after its sha256 has been checked. glibc: CVE-2026-19499 needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer, and no tool here does; CVE-2026-5435 is the deprecated resolver printing functions ns_printrr, ns_printrrf and fp_nquery writing past a caller-supplied buffer when printing TSIG records, which curl, tar and a Rust binary do not call; CVE-2026-84243 is gettext honouring '/' and '..' in LANGUAGE to load a crafted .mo catalogue, which needs a non-C locale, an attacker-controlled environment and a crafted file on disk: the preset sets no locale variable and nothing here places such a file. libstdc++ (gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6): CVE-2026-102010 (erase_if on libstdc++'s binary-heap priority queue, a GNU pb_ds extension in a header-only template, so the flagged packages hold none of it at run time) and CVE-2026-95619 (an integer overflow in the aligned operator new) both need a C++ program, and none of sh, curl, tar, sha256sum (C) or cargo-audit (Rust) is one. Re-argue if the command starts running an affected tool. |

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-80229 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | cargo-audit runs one curl: curl -sSfL -o /tmp/cargo-audit.tgz on a fixed github.com release URL, then checks the archive against a pinned sha256 before tar reads it. The command passes no credentials, proxy, netrc, cookie jar, HSTS file, client certificate, --interface, --proto-default, -J, -w, --aws-sigv4, --crlf, --pinnedpubkey or --parallel, speaks https only, and curl's default redirect protocols are http, https, ftp and ftps; the only server that answers is GitHub's. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest, finding by finding: every one is HIGH, none has a fix at any version, none is in KEV, EPSS at most 0.012. Cookies: CVE-2026-80255 and CVE-2026-82209 (cookie handling) and CVE-2026-92386 (a long cookie record written to a Netscape cookie jar) need the cookie engine, which -b and -c switch on and this command does not. CVE-2026-87862 and CVE-2026-87863 (HSTS import and cache save) need --hsts. Authentication and connection reuse: CVE-2026-8458 (Negotiate connections reused across services), CVE-2026-8932 (client-certificate options left out of the reuse match), CVE-2026-86409 (SigV4 state kept after being unset) and CVE-2026-107929 (CURLOPT_INTERFACE left out of the reuse key) each need an option the command never sets and a handle reused for a second transfer; one handle makes one transfer here. CVE-2026-94266 (credentials in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL) needs credentials in the URL, and the URL carries none. TLS: CVE-2026-80230 (public-key pinning with verification disabled) needs --pinnedpubkey and -k; verification stays on. CVE-2026-9545 (HTTP/3 early data on a cached session) needs --http3 and early data, neither requested. CVE-2026-107928 concerns curl built with GnuTLS sending WebSocket data; the flagged packages are curl and libcurl4t64, Debian's OpenSSL build, and the URL is neither ws:// nor wss://. Other protocols: CVE-2026-13608 (LDAP SASL) and CVE-2026-107161 (Cyrus SASL DIGEST-MD5 client, reached through libcurl's LDAP and mail protocols) need ldap://, imap:// or alike; CVE-2026-87864 (IMAP APPEND with CURLOPT_CRLF), CVE-2026-92387 (control-response timeout of FTP, IMAP, POP3 and SMTP) and CVE-2026-92389 (TFTP state machine) need those servers; CVE-2026-87865 (libssh2 known_hosts), CVE-2026-12064 and CVE-2026-86410 (SSH host verification skipped for a schemeless sftp or scp URL, or after a redirect to one) need an ssh-family transfer: the URL names https, no --proto-default is set, and sftp and scp are outside the default redirect protocols. Tool-only and library-API flaws: CVE-2026-92390 needs --remote-header-name, which the command does not use (it names its output with -o); CVE-2026-9080 (curl_easy_pause inside a CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback), CVE-2026-92391 (a deeply nested MIME tree freed by curl_mime_free) and CVE-2026-80229 (pooled TLS connections outliving their handle) are about an application driving libcurl's API, which the command's single transfer does not. The two CRITICAL curl CVEs this decision used to carry (CVE-2026-18924, CVE-2026-19931) have their own decisions. Re-argue if the command starts using any of these options or protocols. |

| `buildpack-deps:trixie-curl@sha256:9e486725325568707dbd794ca9b53cffb7ddee2b8ac1b94941ca4d3d8c6e9df9` | CVE-2026-88823 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | Unlike the packages in the other decisions, libssl3t64 is used: curl's TLS client opens one https connection to github.com. What each flaw needs is something else. Re-read 2026-11-19 against the scan of the pinned digest: all six are HIGH on openssl, openssl-provider-legacy and libssl3t64 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, not fixed in Debian at any version, none in KEV, EPSS at most 0.006. CVE-2026-107493 needs an application to hand PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex an existing stack and keep using it after a failed read; the PEM it reads here would be the image's own CA bundle, not bytes anyone else chose. CVE-2026-107496 is CMS_encrypt looping on an EC recipient certificate of group order 1; the advisory says TLS and QUIC do not use that path, and nothing here encrypts CMS. CVE-2026-124709 is a QUIC server retaining rejected streams; curl is a client and nothing here listens. CVE-2026-95691 is a use-after-free in the QUIC client on a retransmitted CRYPTO frame, reached only by an HTTP/3 or other QUIC transfer, which needs --http3 and is not requested: the download runs over TCP. CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 are in AES-GCM-SIV, which is not a TLS cipher suite and which no program here calls. Re-argue if the command starts using QUIC, CMS or an OpenSSL application of its own. |

CVE-2026-9545 (HTTP/3 early data on a cached session) needs --http3 and early data, neither requested. CVE-2026-107928 concerns curl built with GnuTLS sending WebSocket data; the flagged packages are curl and libcurl4t64, Debian's OpenSSL build, and the URL is neither ws:// nor wss://. Other protocols: CVE-2026-13608 (LDAP SASL) and CVE-2026-107161 (Cyrus SASL DIGEST-MD5 client, reached through libcurl's LDAP and mail protocols) need ldap://, imap:// or alike; CVE-2026-87864 (IMAP APPEND with CURLOPT_CRLF), CVE-2026-92387 (control-response timeout of FTP, IMAP, POP3 and SMTP) and CVE-2026-92389 (TFTP state machine) need those servers; CVE-2026-87865 (libssh2 known_hosts), CVE-2026-12064 and CVE-2026-86410 (SSH host verification skipped for a schemeless sftp or scp URL, or after a redirect to one) need an ssh-family transfer: the URL names https, no --proto-default is set, and sftp and scp are outside the default redirect protocols. Tool-only and library-API flaws: CVE-2026-92390 needs --remote-header-name, which the command does not use (it names its output with -o); CVE-2026-9080 (curl_easy_pause inside a CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback), CVE-2026-92391 (a deeply nested MIME tree freed by curl_mime_free) and CVE-2026-80229 (pooled TLS connections outliving their handle) are about an application driving libcurl's API, which the command's single transfer does not. OpenSSL (libssl3t64, openssl, openssl-provider-legacy 3.5.7-1~deb13u3+dhi1, EPSS at most 0.006), linked by nothing the preset runs: CVE-2026-107493 (PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex handed an existing stack), CVE-2026-107496 (CMS_encrypt looping on an EC certificate of group order 1), CVE-2026-124709 (a QUIC server retaining rejected streams), CVE-2026-95691 (a use-after-free in the QUIC client), CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 (AES-GCM-SIV AAD and IV handling) each need an application that calls that OpenSSL API or speaks QUIC through it, and the Go programs here use crypto/tls. glibc (libc6 2.41-12+deb13u4+dhi1, EPSS at most 0.003): glibc is linked by the Go CLI, and the flagged paths are not ones Go's runtime uses: CVE-2026-19499 needs strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer; CVE-2026-5435 is the deprecated resolver printers ns_printrr, ns_printrrf and fp_nquery; CVE-2026-84243 is gettext loading a crafted .mo catalogue named through LANGUAGE, which needs a non-C locale, an attacker-controlled environment and a crafted file, and the Go programs do not use gettext. libstdc++ (gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1; EPSS at most 0.005): CVE-2026-102010 (erase_if on a pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template) and CVE-2026-95619 (an integer overflow in the aligned operator new) need a C++ program, and no preset compiles or runs one here. | `ghcr.io/ansible/community-ansible-dev-tools:v26.11.0@sha256:f9caf58a32195c1c2d23cd2ef7f465bc89dd1c6adffa44cd144689b1d41a575a` | CVE-2024-25621 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2026-12-15 | runc, containerd, docker/docker and selinux are vendored into /usr/local/bin/kubectl, which no preset invokes; the vulnerable paths need a container to be run by that binary, and kubectl runs none (docker/docker's flaws are daemon-side handlers -- container archive API, docker cp, the AuthZ plugin -- absent from a client binary). Fixed versions exist at module level and reach us only when the image ships a rebuilt kubectl. Re-argued 2026-09-30 against audit run 36565600041 and a fresh scan of v26.9.0, the newest upstream tag: its kubectl still vendors runc 1.1.13, containerd 1.7.11, docker/docker 27.1.1 and selinux 1.12.0, so no image ships the fix. As decided 2026-08-22 for exactly this case, the treatment is now accepted-risk under the inert model rather than awaiting-upstream -- the blast radius, if inertness is wrong, includes the Docker socket and the Galaxy token -- rather than disabling seven presets over an uninvoked library. The review is a month out on purpose: at each one, scan the newest tag, and if an image has rebuilt kubectl, repin instead of renewing. Reviewed 2026-11-15 by that protocol: the newest upstream tag, ghcr.io/ansible/community-ansible-dev-tools:v26.11.0 (sha256:f9caf58a32195c1c2d23cd2ef7f465bc89dd1c6adffa44cd144689b1d41a575a), was scanned; go version -m on its /usr/local/bin/kubectl (openshift/oc c91286873566, go1.24.13) still shows containerd v1.7.11, docker/docker v27.1.1, runc v1.1.13 and selinux v1.12.0, unchanged. Checked against the commands these presets run; re-argue if they start running the affected tool. |

| `pyfound/black:26.5.1@sha256:bcdafe3e6a60fd181fde19859f7ee4c498557f03bb30af3fa880f502a66e5b5f` | CVE-2025-69720 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2027-01-18 | The vulnerable code sits in the Debian base layer of black's image and is not exercised by what its preset runs: `black --check .` reads the repository's Python files from the mounted workspace, opens no socket, starts no server and runs no other program. Re-read 2026-11-19 against a fresh Trivy and Grype scan of the pinned digest (pyfound/black:26.5.1), member by member; every member below is HIGH, has no fix in either scanner (wont-fix, not-fixed, affected or fix_deferred), and has EPSS at most 0.0063. Members whose fix has since been published (perl, gzip, sqlite, glibc and OpenSSL updates, among them CVE-2026-72897, -84782, -84784 and zlib CVE-2026-85091 that this decision used to carry) were removed from it: they are a repin, not a decision. util-linux (bsdutils and its libraries; CVE-2026-76642, -78408, -78409, -78410): local privilege escalations against mount(8)'s fstab hooks and nsenter, which need an unprivileged local attacker and a privileged (SUID) helper with an authorized fstab entry. A container has no fstab, runs as an unprivileged uid, and the preset runs neither mount nor nsenter. libsystemd0 and libudev1 (CVE-2026-16742): a systemd-homed local privilege escalation; no systemd runs in a container and nothing here talks to it. perl-base: CVE-2026-82560 is CPU exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document, and nothing here runs pod2text or Pod::Text; CVE-2026-9538 is memory exhaustion in Archive::Tar from an attacker-chosen entry size in a tar header, and nothing here runs perl, let alone Archive::Tar on a tar file. glibc: CVE-2026-19499 needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer, which no tool here does; CVE-2026-5435 is an out-of-bounds write in the deprecated resolver printers ns_printrr, ns_printrrf and fp_nquery when printing TSIG records, and Python and black make no DNS query and print no resource records; CVE-2026-84243 lets whoever controls LANGUAGE (and a second locale variable) in a program's environment load a message catalog from an arbitrary path, and needs a crafted .mo file where the program can read it and an environment crossing a trust boundary, as an SSH server accepting client variables does; here the runner sets the environment and the only writable input is the repository's own checkout. ncurses (CVE-2025-69720; libtinfo6, libncursesw6, ncurses-base, ncurses-bin): the overflow is in the infocmp command-line tool (analyze_string in progs/infocmp.c), and nothing here runs infocmp. libacl1 (CVE-2026-54369, -54370): symlink traversal and a check-then-use race in libacl's pathname functions and in getfacl, setfacl and chacl, which matter only to a privileged caller working over a path an attacker controls; the preset runs unprivileged over the user's own checkout and calls none of them. Members whose fix has since been published (perl, gzip, sqlite, glibc and OpenSSL updates, among them CVE-2026-72897, -84782, -84784 and zlib CVE-2026-85091 that this decision used to carry) were removed from it: they are a repin, not a decision. util-linux (bsdutils and its libraries; CVE-2026-76642, -78408, -78409, -78410): local privilege escalations against mount(8)'s fstab hooks and nsenter, which need an unprivileged local attacker and a privileged (SUID) helper with an authorized fstab entry. A container has no fstab, runs as an unprivileged uid, and the preset runs neither mount nor nsenter. libsystemd0 and libudev1 (CVE-2026-16742): a systemd-homed local privilege escalation; no systemd runs in a container and nothing here talks to it. perl-base: CVE-2026-82560 is CPU exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document, and nothing here runs pod2text or Pod::Text; CVE-2026-9538 is memory exhaustion in Archive::Tar from an attacker-chosen entry size in a tar header, and nothing here runs perl, let alone Archive::Tar on a tar file. glibc: CVE-2026-19499 needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer, which no tool here does; CVE-2026-5435 is an out-of-bounds write in the deprecated resolver printers ns_printrr, ns_printrrf and fp_nquery when printing TSIG records, and Python and black make no DNS query and print no resource records; CVE-2026-84243 lets whoever controls LANGUAGE (and a second locale variable) in a program's environment load a message catalog from an arbitrary path, and needs a crafted .mo file where the program can read it and an environment crossing a trust boundary, as an SSH server accepting client variables does; here the runner sets the environment and the only writable input is the repository's own checkout. ncurses (CVE-2025-69720; libtinfo6, libncursesw6, ncurses-base, ncurses-bin): the overflow is in the infocmp command-line tool (analyze_string in progs/infocmp.c), and nothing here runs infocmp. libacl1 (CVE-2026-54369, -54370): symlink traversal and a check-then-use race in libacl's pathname functions and in getfacl, setfacl and chacl, which matter only to a privileged caller working over a path an attacker controls; the preset runs unprivileged over the user's own checkout and calls none of them. SQLite (libsqlite3-0; CVE-2026-119373, -119374, -119379): heap overflows in FTS5 prefix queries on detail=none tables with negative rowids, in FTS5 secure-delete on a crafted index, and in sqlite3changeset_apply on a crafted changeset; each needs a program that opens a database, and black opens none. OpenSSL (libssl3t64, openssl, openssl-provider-legacy): black runs offline, so no TLS handshake of any kind happens in this container. CVE-2026-107493 needs an application passing a non-NULL stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex and reusing it after a failed read, which OpenSSL's own callers never do and nothing here calls. CVE-2026-107496 needs CMS_encrypt to an EC recipient certificate of group order 1, and nothing here encrypts CMS messages. CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 concern AES-GCM-SIV (a zero-length AAD update, a wrong-length IV), an algorithm only the default provider offers, that TLS never selects and no tool here uses. CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; nothing here runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC. gcc and libstdc++ (gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6): CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these runtime packages hold none of it; CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation, and the image runs a Python formatter and no C++ program. Re-argue if the preset starts running any of the affected tools or opens network connections. |

CVE-2026-88823 and CVE-2026-95692 concern AES-GCM-SIV (a zero-length AAD update, a wrong-length IV), an algorithm only the default provider offers, that TLS never selects and no tool here uses. CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; nothing here runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC. gcc and libstdc++ (gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6): CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these runtime packages hold none of it; CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation, and the image runs a Python formatter and no C++ program. Re-argue if the preset starts running any of the affected tools or opens network connections. |

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; no preset runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC (cargo and rustup use HTTP over TLS on TCP). gcc and libstdc++ (cpp-14, gcc-14, gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 and the sanitizer runtimes): the image ships the C toolchain as cargo's linker driver. CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; no preset runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC (cargo and rustup use HTTP over TLS on TCP). gcc and libstdc++ (cpp-14, gcc-14, gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 and the sanitizer runtimes): the image ships the C toolchain as cargo's linker driver. CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these packages hold none of it at run time; it needs a C++ program built with it that calls erase_if. CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation; a Rust build does not use libstdc++ unless the repository's own build script compiles C++ from its own sources, and what such a program allocates is not chosen by an attacker. Re-argue if a preset starts running any of the affected tools, compiles C++ that handles untrusted input, or opens QUIC or server sockets. |

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; no preset runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC (cargo and rustup use HTTP over TLS on TCP). gcc and libstdc++ (cpp-14, gcc-14, gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 and the sanitizer runtimes): the image ships the C toolchain as cargo's linker driver. CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these packages hold none of it at run time; it needs a C++ program built with it that calls erase_if. CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation; a Rust build does not use libstdc++ unless the repository's own build script compiles C++ from its own sources, and what such a program allocates is not chosen by an attacker. Re-argue if a preset starts running any of the affected tools, compiles C++ that handles untrusted input, or opens QUIC or server sockets. |

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; no preset runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC (cargo and rustup use HTTP over TLS on TCP). gcc and libstdc++ (cpp-14, gcc-14, gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 and the sanitizer runtimes): the image ships the C toolchain as cargo's linker driver. CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these packages hold none of it at run time; it needs a C++ program built with it that calls erase_if. CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation; a Rust build does not use libstdc++ unless the repository's own build script compiles C++ from its own sources, and what such a program allocates is not chosen by an attacker. Re-argue if a preset starts running any of the affected tools, compiles C++ that handles untrusted input, or opens QUIC or server sockets. |

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in a QUIC server that rejects a stream and CVE-2026-95691 a use-after-free in a QUIC client fed by a malicious QUIC server; no preset runs a QUIC server or speaks QUIC (cargo and rustup use HTTP over TLS on TCP). gcc and libstdc++ (cpp-14, gcc-14, gcc-14-base, libgcc-s1, libstdc++6 and the sanitizer runtimes): the image ships the C toolchain as cargo's linker driver. CVE-2026-102010 is a use-after-free in erase_if on libstdc++'s pb_ds binary-heap priority queue, a header-only template instantiated into an application at build time, so these packages hold none of it at run time; it needs a C++ program built with it that calls erase_if. CVE-2026-95619 is an integer overflow in the aligned operator new, which needs a C++ program asking for an attacker-sized aligned allocation; a Rust build does not use libstdc++ unless the repository's own build script compiles C++ from its own sources, and what such a program allocates is not chosen by an attacker. Re-argue if a preset starts running any of the affected tools, compiles C++ that handles untrusted input, or opens QUIC or server sockets. |
